hints.lin.functions.evaluate: f(3) means: put 3 in for x in the rule. Negative inputs go in parentheses.
hints.lin.functions.table: Find how much y changes each time x goes up 1. Then count the steps to the x you want.
hints.lin.functions: f(3): put 3 in for x. Tables: find the change for each step, then count steps.
hints.lin.functions.linear: Linear means the rate is the same: change in y ÷ change in x is the same between every pair of rows. An equation with x² isn't linear.

misconceptionMessages.lin.f-input-output: Here you know the OUTPUT, f(x) = 11. Set the rule equal to 11 and solve for x.
misconceptionMessages.lin.f-sign: Keep the input's minus sign: put it in with parentheses. f(−2) with f(x) = 3x + 1 is 3(−2) + 1 = −5.
misconceptionMessages.lin.table-swapped: The question asks for y, the output. Find the pattern in the y row.
misconceptionMessages.lin.table-add-step: Count how many steps x jumps, and add the change that many times, not just once.
misconceptionMessages.lin.nonlinear-increasing: Going up isn't enough: in a linear table y goes up by the same amount for each step in x. Check the changes.
misconceptionMessages.lin.nonlinear-power: x² makes it curve: the changes in y grow. Linear equations have x only to the first power (y = mx + b).
misconceptionMessages.lin.uneven-x-steps: Look at how far x jumps too. Divide each change in y by its change in x; linear means that's the same every time.

sections.title: Function notation
sections.objective: Find f(3) for a rule like f(x) = 2x + 5.
explain: f(x) = 2x + 5 is a rule: put in an x, get out a y.
f(3) means the output when the input is 3.
sections.key: f(3) means: put 3 in for x in the rule and work it out. f(3) is the output; 3 is the input.

sections.title: Tables
sections.objective: Read and extend an x/y table.
explain: In a linear table, y changes by the same amount every time x goes up 1.
Count the steps to the x you want.

sections.title: Linear or not?
sections.objective: Tell whether a table or an equation is linear.
explain: A linear function changes at a constant rate: the same change in y for each step in x. Its graph is a straight line.
Equations like y = 3x − 2 are linear; y = x² + 1 is not.
sections.key: Linear means a constant rate: change in y ÷ change in x is the same between every pair of rows. x² (or x in the bottom) means not linear.

worked.note: x jumps by 2 in the middle
